Guided Tours in Chattanooga, TN

This guide covers 13 guided tours in and around Chattanooga. The options range from city history and ghost tours to outdoor adventures, cave spelunking, and food walks.
Nickajack Cave near South Pittsburg holds up to 100,000 gray bats. The Bat Cave Sunset Kayak Tour lets you watch them emerge at dusk. It is one of the more unusual things you can do within an hour of downtown.
Nine of the 13 tours depart from or near downtown. Chattanooga Ducks, Rydables, and Ghost Tours all leave from near the riverfront. Several can be combined in a single day without a car.
The Outdoor filter surfaces five adventure-based options. The Type filter separates city history from outdoor tours and food experiences. The Day Trip filter shows three options that require a short drive outside of Chattanooga.
If there is a tour worth adding, send an email. Details change. Confirm before you go.

City & History Tours.

Six tours in this guide cover Chattanooga’s history. The Trolley Tours give the broadest city overview. Ghost Tours and the Guided Walking Tour move slower and go deeper. Chickamauga adds a 15-minute drive but covers the second most deadly Civil War battle in the country. The Duck Boat and Rydables are lighter on history but cover the same downtown geography.

History museums and exhibits

Outdoor Tours.

Five options here get you outside the city. The Bat Cave Kayak runs on the Tennessee River near South Pittsburg from March through October. Experience Chattanooga runs private hikes across the region’s mountain trails. Raccoon Mountain Caverns is 8 miles west and open daily. Lookout Mountain Flight Park is for the person who wants something they will talk about for years.

Outdoor adventures guideCloudland Canyon guide

Good for Kids.

Four tours here work well for families. The Duck Boat is the most reliably fun option for mixed ages. The Southern Belle has sightseeing and dinner options that fit all ages. Experience Chattanooga’s alpaca hike is a popular pick for younger kids. Raccoon Mountain Caverns has a lit-path walking tour for all ages, plus more intense wild cave options for older kids and adults.

Kid-friendly exhibits

Day Trips.

Three tours require a short drive. Nickajack Cave (Bat Cave Kayak) is about 35 miles west in South Pittsburg, TN. Chickamauga Battlefield is 15 minutes south in Fort Oglethorpe, GA. Lookout Mountain Flight Park is 30 minutes in Rising Fawn, GA. The Bat Cave tour runs only March through October, so check the season before planning.

Clear filters

1. Chattanooga Trolley Tours .

Vintage red and green trolley tours through downtown Chattanooga led by local guides. Tour lengths range from one to four hours depending on the option. Four tours include the Derailed Adventure (~$49), Legends and Shadows (~$32), Express Trolley (~$29), and Coker Museum and Trolley (~$42). The vehicle is air-conditioned and enclosed. Private tours are available with advance booking. Rated 4.9 stars on Google.

#city-history #indoor #downtown #kids

2. Chattanooga Ghost Tours .

Walking tours through downtown Chattanooga focused on haunted history and local folklore. Three options: Murder and Mayhem Haunted History walk (2 hours), UTC Cemetery Ghost Hunt (1.5 hours, equipment included), and a Walk and Hunt Combo. Extended Deluxe tours with refreshment stops at haunted locations run on select dates. The tours draw on the city's Civil War history and Trail of Tears past. Tours run rain or shine.
Google Maps Website
#city-history #walking #downtown

3. Chattanooga Ducks .

Restored WWII amphibious Duck vehicle that tours downtown streets and then drives into the Tennessee River. The narrated tour runs about one hour and covers downtown, the riverfront, and Maclellan Island wildlife sanctuary. Tours depart from 151 Riverfront Parkway and start around $36 per person. Works for all ages. Book ahead on busy weekends.
Google Maps Website
#city-history #water #outdoor #downtown #kids

4. Chattanooga Rydables .

Guided tours on motorized scooters across the Walnut Street Bridge and through downtown. Some scooters are themed as unicorns and dragons. A guide leads the group and provides history and trivia along the route. The Bridge to Fun one-hour ride starts around $55. The From Trains to Bridges 1.5-hour tour (includes the Choo Choo) runs about $75. Tours run seven days a week and sell out.
Google Maps Website
#city-history #outdoor #downtown

5. Chattanooga Guided Walking Tour .

A 90-minute history walk through downtown led by local author and historian J.D. Harper. The route covers Ross's Landing, the Tennessee Riverwalk, the Tennessee Aquarium, the Historic Read House, and the Tivoli Theatre. Tours meet at the Chattanooga Visitor Center at 215 Broad Street. Tickets start around $23 per adult. Groups cap at 25 people.
Google Maps Website
#city-history #walking #downtown

6. Bat Cave Sunset Kayak Tour .

Guided kayak trip to watch up to 100,000 gray bats emerge from Nickajack Cave at sunset. The 3-mile route is beginner-friendly with no prior kayaking experience needed. Tours run March through early October, starting around 7:30pm from Maple View Recreation Area in South Pittsburg, TN. The tour lasts about 2 hours and costs around $77 per person. Groups of up to 20 people welcome. Rated 5.0 stars.
Google Maps Website
#outdoor #water #seasonal #day-trip

7. Chickamauga Battlefield Tours .

The site of the second most deadly Civil War battle, 15 minutes from downtown in Fort Oglethorpe, GA. Ranger-led tours run on weekends at 10am and 2pm and last about 90 minutes. The NPS app provides a self-guided tour of eight points of interest across the 5,000-acre park. The visitors center has artifacts, a relief map, and an orientation film. Private tours with local historian Robert Carter are also available. Admission is free.
Google Maps Website
#city-history #outdoor #day-trip #near-georgia

8. Experience Chattanooga Hikes .

Private guided hikes run by two lifelong Chattanoogans with nearly 200 five-star reviews. Options include panoramic mountain hikes, waterfall trails, and a tour that includes a stop at Rosie Mae's Alpaca Farm. Professional photography is included with every booking. The company donates a portion of proceeds to local parks and communities. All tours are private.
Google Maps Website
#outdoor #kids #adventure

9. Raccoon Mountain Caverns .

Living cave about 8 miles west of downtown with guided tours through stalactites, flowstone, and cave formations. The Crystal Palace Walking Tour is a 45-55 minute lit-path walk priced around $29 for adults and $19 for kids. Wild Cave tours provide a helmet and light for deeper exploration: 2-hour ($35), 3-hour ($45), and 4-hour ($55) expeditions. Open daily.
Google Maps Website
#outdoor #adventure #kids #west-chattanooga

10. Lookout Mountain Hang Gliding .

Tandem hang gliding with a certified instructor at Lookout Mountain Flight Park. An ultralight plane tows you to 1,500 or 3,000 feet, then you soar over the mountain. Discovery flights start around $199. Requirements: at least 14 years old and under 250 pounds. The park is at 7201 Scenic Highway in Rising Fawn, GA, about 30 minutes from downtown.
Google Maps Website
#outdoor #adventure #day-trip #near-georgia

11. Trolley Pub Chattanooga .

Pedal-powered group tour through downtown with stops at local bars. BYOB and connect to onboard Bluetooth speakers with your own playlist. The guide calls out landmarks along the route. Private tours fit up to 14 people and run $300-375. Public Mixer Tours are $25-30 per person and are 21+. Private tours allow ages 15+. Tours run rain or shine.
Google Maps Website
#food-entertainment #outdoor #downtown

12. Southern Belle Riverboat .

Historic paddlewheel riverboat that travels the Tennessee River on narrated sightseeing and dining cruises. Options include a 1.5-hour Sunset Cruise (~$36), a Sights Cruise, a Sip and Sail dinner cruise with wine pairings, and eco tours to Maclellan Island. The vessel departs from the downtown riverfront. Works for families, date nights, and groups.
Google Maps Website
#food-entertainment #water #downtown #kids

13. Chatt Taste Food Tours .

Guided walking food tours through downtown Chattanooga and the Historic Southside. Three tour options: Downtown Chattanooga Food Tour, Historic Southside Food Tour (2 hours), and ChattaBrunch (food, art, history, and mimosas). Private tours and events are also available. Rated 5.0 stars, with reviewers praising knowledgeable and friendly hosts.

Most downtown tours run on the same day. Book the ones that sell out first: Chattanooga Ducks and Rydables fill up on weekends. Ghost Tours and the Guided Walking Tour are easier to get into day-of.
If you plan an outdoor day trip, the Bat Cave Kayak and Chickamauga Battlefield are both best on weekdays. The Bat Cave tour runs only March through October. For more self-guided outdoor options, see the Chattanooga outdoors guide.

FAQ.

Are there ghost tours in Chattanooga?

Yes. Chattanooga Ghost Tours runs walking tours and ghost hunts downtown. The Murder and Mayhem Haunted History walk covers downtown in 2 hours. The UTC Cemetery Ghost Hunt lasts 1.5 hours and includes ghost hunting equipment. A combined Walk and Hunt tour is also available. Tours run rain or shine for all ages.

How much is the Chattanooga Ducks tour?

The Chattanooga Ducks tour starts around $36 per person. The tour lasts about one hour and departs from 151 Riverfront Parkway downtown. The Duck drives through downtown streets and then into the Tennessee River. Book ahead on busy weekends as tours sell out.

Can you kayak to Nickajack Cave near Chattanooga?

Yes. Chattanooga Guided Adventures runs a guided sunset kayak tour to Nickajack Cave from March through early October. Up to 100,000 gray bats emerge from the cave at dusk. The 3-mile route is beginner-friendly with no prior experience needed. Tours start around $77 and meet at Maple View Recreation Area in South Pittsburg, TN.

What food tours are available in Chattanooga?

Chatt Taste offers three guided food tours: the Downtown Chattanooga Food Tour, the Historic Southside Food Tour (2 hours), and ChattaBrunch (food, art, history, and mimosas). Private tours and events are also available. All are walking tours led by local guides with 5-star ratings.

Is Chickamauga Battlefield free to visit?

Yes. Chickamauga Battlefield is a National Park and admission is free. Ranger-guided tours run on weekends at 10am and 2pm and last about 90 minutes. The NPS app provides a self-guided driving or walking tour of eight points of interest. The battlefield is in Fort Oglethorpe, GA, about 15 minutes from downtown Chattanooga.

How much does hang gliding near Chattanooga cost?

Lookout Mountain Flight Park offers tandem hang gliding from Rising Fawn, GA, about 30 minutes from downtown. Discovery flights start around $199 per person. You must be at least 14 years old and under 250 pounds. An ultralight plane tows you to 1,500 or 3,000 feet before you soar on your own.
